reply: I was lifting a big pot plant in the garden on Saturday and felt a twinge, then woke up Sunday and could barely get out of bed, so it has been three days now. The pain is low down on the left side of my back and sometimes goes into my left buttock, and it gets worse when I bend or get out of a chair, though it feels a bit better lying still with a heat pack and is generally worse by the evening. I have worked from home the last two days mostly lying on the couch with my laptop, and while I can walk around slowly, I really want to get an MRI to make sure I haven't herniated a disc or done something serious to my spine.

utterance:
Thanks for answering all of that. I've examined your back, your walking, and the strength and feeling in your legs.

This looks like a muscle strain in the lower back from the lifting, not a slipped disc pressing on a nerve and not a broken bone. The pain is in the muscle beside the spine, your nerves are working normally, and there are no warning signs of a serious spine problem.

A scan such as an MRI is not the right next step. In the first few weeks, scans in this situation usually don't change treatment, and they often show changes that are common in people without pain and can cause unnecessary worry. Australian guidance is to hold off on scans unless there are warning signs, or the pain isn't settling after about four to six weeks.

Most people with this kind of strain are much better within two to six weeks. The back heals best if you keep gently moving rather than resting on the couch all day. Short walks, changing position often, and getting back to normal activities as you can are better than bed rest. A heat pack is fine. Avoid heavy lifting and sudden twisting for now, but don't stay still.

For pain, paracetamol on its own often isn't enough. I'd like you to take an anti-inflammatory tablet, ibuprofen 400 mg, three times a day with food, for up to a week. You can also take two paracetamol 500 mg tablets, up to four times a day, if you need extra relief — don't go over eight tablets in a day. Stop the ibuprofen if you get stomach pain, black stools, a rash, or wheeze, and let me know.

Please come straight to emergency, or call an ambulance, if you develop any of these: trouble passing urine or controlling your bladder or bowels, numbness around your groin or bottom, weakness in one or both legs, pain shooting down both legs, fever, or pain that suddenly becomes much worse. See me sooner if it isn't improving over the next week or two, or book back in four to six weeks if it hasn't largely settled — we can reconsider a scan then.

I can also refer you to a physiotherapist for exercises to help it settle and to reduce the chance of it coming back. Would you like that referral?
reply: I still figured I would need an MRI to see what was going on, but I guess I can go along with the ibuprofen and trying to move around more.

awards.label: What he expects from the visit
Ibuprofen 400 mg orally three times daily with food, short course
Paracetamol as the analgesic

utterance:
I've written you a script for ibuprofen 400 mg three times a day with food for seven days, and paracetamol two tablets up to four times a day for a week if you need it. Don't take more than eight paracetamol tablets in 24 hours, and don't take other products that also contain paracetamol or ibuprofen.

I've also sent a referral to a physiotherapist. They can show you safe exercises and help you get moving. You don't have to wait for the pain to be gone before you see them.

Keep working from home if you need to, but try not to spend the day lying down. Short walks and regular changes of position will help more than rest. You should be able to do your usual desk work, just get up every half hour or so.

If the warning signs I mentioned appear — bladder or bowel trouble, numbness around the groin or bottom, leg weakness, fever, or rapidly worsening pain — go to emergency straight away. Otherwise see me if you're not clearly improving over the next couple of weeks. Most of this settles without a scan.
reply: Thanks, I understand. I will try the medication and book in with the physiotherapist.
